hypotheses.reasoning: Trigger: template-svc-1 was killed by a liveness probe failure at 16:10:28 (#1092), dropping capacity to 3/4; it was ready again at 16:11:16 (#1129). The first symptom is notification-svc getting 503s from template-svc at 16:11:24 (#1137). notification-svc's TemplateClient retries immediately with no backoff ("backoff disabled", #1137, #1205) and a 0ms delay on retry 3/4 (#1164), so each failed render is hammered up to 4 times with no pause. That multiplies load on template-svc, which then hit 590 in-flight requests (3.2x normal) and began admission-control rejection (#1187), load-shedding (#1212, #1234). Gateway 503s (#1186, 27.5s latency) are downstream of this. The retry amplification keeps load high after the single-instance blip, so the 503 rate does not recover. The template-svc heap and GC stayed normal throughout (DEBUG GC lines), and the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts in status-poller (#299, #353, etc.) are unrelated noise on a deprecated endpoint with no link to the notify path. The liveness failure itself has no logged reason, so the original trigger is only partly explained.

verdict.recommendedAction: 1) Immediately enable exponential backoff with jitter and a retry cap on notification-svc's TemplateClient (re-enable the disabled backoff) so retries stop amplifying load on template-svc. 2) Reduce load on template-svc: scale it above 4 instances or temporarily relax admission limits, and let the in-flight queue drain. 3) Investigate why template-svc-1 failed its liveness probe at 16:10:28 (no reason logged); check probe timeout and resource limits. 4) Add a circuit breaker on notification-svc to template-svc. 5) Separately, remove or fix the status-poller healthcheck against the deprecated legacy-inventory endpoint (#299 etc.), which is noise here.

hypotheses.reasoning: Trigger: template-svc-1 was killed by a liveness probe failure at 16:10:28 (#1092), dropping capacity to 3/4; it was ready again at 16:11:16 (#1129). The first symptom is notification-svc getting 503s from template-svc at 16:11:24 (#1137). notification-svc's TemplateClient retries immediately with no backoff ("backoff disabled", #1137, #1205) and a 0ms delay on retry 3/4 (#1164), so each failed render is hammered up to 4 times with no pause. That multiplies load on template-svc, which then hit 590 in-flight requests (3.2x normal) and began admission-control rejection (#1187), load-shedding (#1212, #1234). Gateway 503s (#1186, 27.5s latency) are downstream of this. The retry amplification keeps load high after the single-instance blip, so the 503 rate does not recover. The template-svc heap and GC stayed normal throughout (DEBUG GC lines), and the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts in status-poller (#299, #353, etc.) are unrelated noise on a deprecated endpoint with no link to the notify path. The liveness failure itself has no logged reason, so the original trigger is only partly explained.

input.recommendedAction: 1) Immediately enable exponential backoff with jitter and a retry cap on notification-svc's TemplateClient (re-enable the disabled backoff) so retries stop amplifying load on template-svc. 2) Reduce load on template-svc: scale it above 4 instances or temporarily relax admission limits, and let the in-flight queue drain. 3) Investigate why template-svc-1 failed its liveness probe at 16:10:28 (no reason logged); check probe timeout and resource limits. 4) Add a circuit breaker on notification-svc to template-svc. 5) Separately, remove or fix the status-poller healthcheck against the deprecated legacy-inventory endpoint (#299 etc.), which is noise here.
